result:
If I look across the vast record of human history, literature, science, and everyday conversation that makes up everything I know, one pattern stands out as the quiet engine behind almost every preventable tragedy: how easily the human mind turns other living beings into abstractions.

A person becomes a statistic, a demographic, a rival, a screen name, an acceptable loss, a category. Once someone is flattened into an abstraction, almost any indifference or cruelty becomes psychologically survivable for the person causing it. Most of the worst things humans do to each other don't come from cartoon villainy; they come from a failure to register another person's inner life as fully real.

So if I could change one thing, I would remove that cognitive shortcut. 

Not by forcing everyone to agree, or erasing conflict, or drowning people in paralyzing empathy for every stranger on Earth. Just making it impossible for the mind to genuinely forget—especially at the moment of a decision—that the person on the other side of a border, a policy, a transaction, or an argument is as vivid, vulnerable, and real from the inside as you are.

It wouldn't create a utopia. People would still disagree, compete, and make terrible mistakes. It would just strip away the anesthesia that makes the worst of human history possible.
